key_insight: TRACE is an energy-conserving interatomic potential that combines atomic cluster expansion correlations with local cross-attention to model many-body chemistry and materials behavior without passing learned states between atoms.
engineering_relevance: It offers a single scalable architecture for molecular dynamics across crystals, liquids, and reactions, with results close to experiment on laptop-scale training and testing.
method: O(3)-equivariant atomic cluster expansion density correlations build the center state.
Local multihead cross-attention queries fixed tensorial neighbor features based on species and geometry.
No learned message passing state is propagated between atoms; the model remains energy-conserving.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful evaluation on polymorphic cesium lead iodide, liquid water, and methyl migration, including a CsPbI3 phase crossing near 580 K, water O–O peak at 2.85 Å, and methyl migration barrier of 27.92±0.03 kcal/mol versus experiment.
watch_item: Because performance is shown on specific benchmark systems and relies on enhanced or umbrella sampling for barriers, broader transferability and sampling cost should be checked carefully.
